requirement.original: The user says OOM kills DO happen regularly on this server. We need to understand the EXACT timing pattern of OOM kills to distinguish them from manual archive operations.
requirement.clarified: Characterize session death patterns on this server including timing, count, and causes to enable reliable classification of events in the session watcher.
requirement.what: Investigation and characterization of session death timing patterns
requirement.why: The session recovery watcher needs to distinguish OOM/crash events from manual archives to avoid unnecessary restore triggers
success_criteria: Clear characterization of each session death pattern type
Timing parameters for each pattern documented
Reliable distinguishing criteria between OOM, manual archive, natural exit, and reboot

root_cause_analysis.symptom: User reports OOM kills happen regularly
root_cause_analysis.root_cause: NO cgroup OOM kills have ever occurred on this server. All cgroup memory.events counters are zero. Session deaths are caused by: (1) server reboots, (2) natural process exits, (3) crash-loop sessions that die on resume, (4) dev workspace cleanups
root_cause_analysis.why_problematic: Misattributing session deaths to OOM leads to wrong watcher thresholds and unnecessary recovery logic complexity

investigation_findings.kernel_oom: No kernel OOM events in dmesg or journalctl

reboot_kill.description: All sessions die in same second after server reboot
distinguishing_features: Preceded by systemd restart logs ~3min earlier

cascade_kill.description: Same session repeatedly dies and gets restored
distinguishing_features: Same UUID in alternating remove/add pattern
Isolated in time (minutes/hours gap to next)
Not followed by immediate re-death after restore
May be memory pressure or coincidence

dev_batch_kill.description: Multiple dev workspace sessions killed together
distinguishing_features: All sessions from same directory (dev workspace)

research_findings.reason: Direct empirical investigation of server data, no external research needed

development_approach.strategy: Use findings to inform watcher threshold design
development_approach.validation_approach: Cross-reference future session deaths against this characterization
